fields.rationale: States cluster by how demanding and specific their reciprocity conditions are: some require only equivalent standards, others add significant practice-hour minimums, others mandate additional state exams, some delegate everything to board discretion, a few offer an expedited or endorsement-style path, and a handful provide only a bare-bones statutory statement.

assignments.raw_value: Applicant must be a graduate of a board-recognized optometry school; pass Alaska law exam; hold current equivalent license in another US state/territory or Canadian province; have previously passed the NBEO; have at least 3,120 hours of active clinical practice in the preceding 36 months; have no disciplinary history; and have received adequate pain management/opioid education (unless no DEA number).

Applicant must have passed a standard examination in optometry in another state or all parts of the NBEO exam, hold a current license in any U.S. state, and have conducted an ethical professional practice for at least one year. At board discretion, applicant pays the regular examination fee and must pass the Alabama standard examination.

Must be qualified under the chapter; have a license from a state/territory/DC/Canada with standards equal to Arkansas; have practiced lawfully for 3 of the past 4 years; pass Arkansas jurisprudence exam; submit required documents including criminal background check.

Applicant must hold a valid license from another U.S. jurisdiction with equivalent requirements, not have had license suspended or revoked, have practiced optometry continuously for at least 4 of the 5 years preceding application, and be verified by national data banks.

Applicant must hold a doctor of optometry degree from an accredited school, have passed a licensing exam in another state, be licensed in good standing in all states where licensed, not be subject to disciplinary action, pass the California jurisprudence examination, meet continuing education requirements, and meet TPA certification requirements.

Applicant must satisfy the requirements of the occupational credential portability program, which includes demonstrating substantially equivalent experience or credentials and holding a current valid license in another jurisdiction for at least one year.

Applicant must hold a license from another state/territory with equivalent or higher requirements, or a CELMO certificate from ARBO. Fee of $565. No license issued if disciplinary action is pending or unresolved complaint exists.

Applicant must hold a valid license from another jurisdiction, have practiced for a minimum of 5 years in that jurisdiction under standards equal to or greater than Delaware's, contact the National Practitioner Data Bank for verification, and obtain certified statements from all jurisdictions where previously or currently licensed confirming no pending disciplinary proceedings or unresolved complaints.
The board may enter into reciprocity agreements with other states to ensure that licensed practitioners may be considered for licensure in other states.

assignments.raw_value: "optometry" means the examination, evaluation, diagnosis, treatment, or performance of preventive procedures related to diseases, disorders, or conditions of the human eyes or adjacent and associated structures, consistent with this chapter and regulations adopted by the board

The practice of optometry is a learned profession involving the examination, measurement by objective and subjective means, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of any departure from the normal of the human eyes, their adjacent structures, and visual system.

The 'practice of optometry' means the examination, diagnosis, treatment, and management of conditions of the human eye, lid, adnexa, and visual system, including the removal of foreign bodies from the cornea, conjunctiva, lid, or adnexa but shall exclude other surgery of the lid, adnexa, or visual system which requires anything other than a topical anesthetic.
